desc: Derive correct characterization: valid graphs = connected graphs whose BFS layers from vertex 1 have balanced parity; edges allowed within a layer and between adjacent layers only; each vertex in layer i+1 needs ≥1 neighbor in layer i; GF factorizes per layer-size sequence; verified by hand against sample 1 (12 9 3 0).

Reference implementation: DP over states (u=vertices used, d=balance, a=last layer size, p=layer parity) with transition adding layer size b: multiply by C(N-1-u,b)·((1+x)^a-1)^b·(1+x)^{C(b,2)}, polynomials truncated to C(N,2); answer = sum of f[N-1][0][a][p]. Includes |d2| ≤ remaining pruning.

Validate reference on samples N=4 (`12 9 3 0`), N=6 (`810 2100 3060 3030 2230 1210 450 100 10 0 0`), N=10 — all match exactly. Edge cases confirmed by model: min degree N-1 automatic, trailing zeros printed.
Profile N=30: 1,081,227 transitions, conv_work ≈ 1.3×10^9 mod-multiplies, ~47s pure Python → numpy batching essential; strategy chosen: batched split-FFT per (u,a,b) group.

Implement numpy batched-FFT version: group states by (u, a, p, b), stack (d,p)-polys into 2D int64 arrays, split lo/hi (15-bit), rfft(axis=1), multiply by cached kernel FFTs (4 products → 3 irfft), round, recombine mod P, scatter-add into target (u+b, d2, b, p^1). Kernels computed exactly with Python big-int convolutions then reduced mod P; adaptive FFT size per group.
Validate numpy version on all three samples (exact match), N=2 → `1`, and cross-check vs reference for small N — split-FFT rounding confirmed exact (magnitudes < 2^51 < 2^53).
Profile numpy version: N=30 ≈ 6–9s; bottleneck is per-group Python/numpy overhead (~40k groups: array building, 3 irffts, per-row np.nonzero, dict scatter-add), not the FFTs themselves.

Apply micro-optimizations: merge p=0/p=1 into one batch per (u,a,b); preallocate F buffer; direct int64 convolution path for tiny groups (R·maxlen·lk below threshold); vectorized trim (argmax on reversed) and grouped scatter-add; scipy.fft with np.fft fallback.
Re-measure N=30 wall time after optimizations (target < 2s); if still too slow, batch across u for fixed (a,b) with per-u target demux.
Regression-test after each change: all three samples + N=2 + random small-N cross-checks against the reference implementation.
Finalize: fast stdin/stdout, remove instrumentation, confirm code reads N P and writes single-line space-separated answers mod P.
